title: POST /game-api/s2s-api/v1.0/lobby/rooms/acceptPlayer
$comment: Observed on 1.8.0.13 with a real player joining from the same machine: 200, 979 bytes, twice. This answer is everything the dedicated server learns about the player in one shot - profile, account links and the career record - and the career record never travels back (see section 3.0 of docs/en/ArmaReforger_BackendAPI_EN.md). The ids and the career values in the example are placeholders; the structure, the field names and the array length are the captured ones.

sessionTicket.description: The ticket for this one join. The server passes it through untranslated; where the client got it was not observed, because the client was not behind the proxy.

userId.description: Equal to character.id and to the identityId the server logs for the join.

username.description: Empty in the capture; the display name arrives in platformUsername instead.

renameCount.description: -1 in the capture; -1 is the value the backend uses rather than a real count.

currencies.description: The two currency balances. The key order differs between the two captured answers - irrelevant to JSON, but it is why the examples are not byte-identical.

countryCode.description: ISO country of the player as the backend sees it. Observed: RU.

overallPlayTime.description: Seconds of career play time. Observed: 79271.

entries.description: Empty in the capture; the element shape is not observed.

visitedGames.description: Empty in the capture; the element shape is not observed.

name.description: The player's current in-game name, which the capture shows as the same name the server logs.

version.description: A big integer, 1771950693478825984 in the capture - larger than 2^53, so a JSON reader that goes through a double will lose precision. It is presumably the record's version/etag for the write that never happens.

data.description: A JSON document inside a string. Parsed, it is {"m_aStats":[ ... ]} with one number per SCR_EDataStats member - 39 of them on this build. See docs/en/ArmaReforger_Profile_EN.md section 5, where the 39 positions are broken down.

biAccountId.description: The player's linked Bohemia account. **Present on the wire only**: the string biAccountId appears in neither ArmaReforgerServer.exe nor ArmaReforgerSteam.exe 1.8.0.13, so no engine class declares this field and it is dropped when the JSON is expanded into script objects - the same fate as the blacklist/whitelist/admins arrays the backend warns about. This schema describes the answer, not what the engine keeps.

steamId.description: The player's SteamID64, as a decimal string - the raw platform id. Its console counterparts in the binary are named xboxIdHash and psnIdHash, i.e. hashes rather than ids; no console player was captured. Section 5 of docs/en/ArmaReforger_BackendAPI_EN.md says what an identity can and cannot be resolved to.

platformIdentities.description: Which store and account the player came from. Present for a player who is in the session; no endpoint that resolves an identityId to this without one was observed.

platformUsername.description: The platform-side display name. Observed: the same name that appears in the ban records and in the server log.
